description: LUNAR FRONTIER is a student-led team building a 3D lunar exploration and mission simulation game for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Players will explore the Moon, collect scientific samples, deploy research equipment, build a lunar outpost, manage power and life-support systems, conduct greenhouse experiments, and solve engineering challenges. We welcome teammates interested in Unreal Engine 5, C++, coding, 3D modelling, game design, UI/UX, science research, and storytelling.
summary: ORBITAL is a free, first-person browser game that trains students like junior astronauts. Players float outside a space station wearing a helmet visor with a live HUD for oxygen, jetpack fuel and mission time. They complete three missions: repairing cracks in a station, catching floating debris, and getting through an airlock. Each mission ends with a quiz based on real NASA missions and science. It makes space science feel like a real spacewalk, with no download or special hardware.
details:
What it does: ORBITAL is a first-person space training game that runs in any modern browser. The player sees through an astronaut helmet visor, with 3D gloves, a jetpack and a holographic HUD showing oxygen, jetpack fuel and a mission timer.

How it works: There are three missions. In Spacewalk, the player finds and repairs cracks on a station while the oxygen counts down. In Debris, the player uses the jetpack to catch 12 floating fragments, which teaches why orbital debris is dangerous. In Airlock, the player flies into an airlock ring and holds position for 5 seconds. After each mission, a quiz explains the real science, and a mission report shows time, oxygen, fuel, quiz score and a 1 to 3 star rating.

Benefits and goal: Space science is often taught from slides. ORBITAL lets students feel the pressure of limited oxygen, fuel and time while they learn why astronauts follow these procedures. We hope it inspires young learners to explore space careers.

Tools: Three.js (WebGL), JavaScript, Vite, HTML/CSS/SVG for the helmet visor, Web Audio API for sound effects, glTF/GLB 3D models, and Blender for model preparation.

NASA data
The quiz and mission design are based on public NASA information about:

  • The International Space Station: orbit of about 400 km altitude, speed of about 28,000 km/h, and about 90 minutes per orbit.
  • Spacewalks, spacesuits and airlock procedures, including pre-breathing.
  • The OSIRIS-REx mission, which launched in 2016 and returned its Bennu asteroid sample in September 2023.
  • The ICESat-2 mission, which launched in 2018 and measures ice height with the ATLAS laser.
  • Orbital debris and the Kessler Syndrome.
  • Space agency partner and other data
  • Three.js (MIT license), Vite (MIT license).
